location_qualifier: off Cape Esperance, mined and scuttled
source_locator: R2250: C08030022900, 經過, ソロモン方面, 1–2 February 1943 (PDF pp. 21–22). R2242: 2 February 1943
current_activity: mined off Cape Esperance during the first Ke-Go lift and scuttled
notes: JACAR 8th Fleet February 經過 (C08030022900, PDF pp. 21–22) records 巻雲揚陸作業中觸雷沈没 in the 1 February (二―一) first Ke-Go lift at エスペ, and on the next page that an attempt to take her in tow was abandoned and she was disposed of. Cressman, 2 February 1943, states that Makigumo was damaged by a mine laid off Cape Esperance the previous night and was scuttled by Yugumo at 09°10'S, 159°45'E. The claim is dated 2 February, Cressman's calendar date for the scuttling (the mine hit was during the night of 1–2). Place is Ironbottom Sound (area), qualifier off Cape Esperance, so two official families can reach 0.7; a separate sea_position pin was not added. Yugumo is not clearly named as the scuttling ship in the JACAR pages read and is not entered. Confidence 0.7: JACAR (jacar) and Cressman (us_navy_nhhc) agree she was mined and lost off Cape Esperance in that night action.
